digest.component_or_area: janitor plan recovery and approval; binding store, lifecycle reconciliation, operation configuration, CLI registry, and plan-review policy
propositions: Five recovered RP-02 through RP-06 design decisions require evidence-backed research, durable briefs, and maintainer approval before becoming implementation stories; RP-02 transaction atomicity and recovery semantics, RP-03 Jira failure/retry classification and fuse policy, RP-04 operation configuration precedence and secret boundary, RP-05 CLI registry lazy loading and help normalization, and RP-06 plan-review applicability routing and checkpoint failure handling are the architectural checkpoints.

RP-02 must own ordered exact-match retirement recovery at a validated live-operation boundary with read-only construction/preview, separate lifecycle-policy/recovery/repository owners, and narrow closure of the production all_bindings mutation leak; RP-03 consumes the coherent post-recovery snapshot and owns TicketPlan orchestration without duplicating binding persistence.

RP-03 establishes singular retry ownership separating concrete adapter request-replay/timeouts from backend-neutral reconciler operation intent/postconditions, commit_unknown, re-observation, dependency deferral, and scoped finite-pass fuse; Jira rate scopes are ticket-local, endpoint-family, tenant/global quota, or unknown; defaults are 3 physical attempts and 15 seconds cumulative sleep per logical operation.

RP-04 implements explicit > environment > project > user > default precedence per operation, separate secret/provider boundary, non-secret subprocess envelope, central defaults, and removal of Cloud adapter-local DIG fallback; RP-05 chooses between normalizing all 21 advanced verbs onto side-effect-free help or preserving current two-family policy; RP-06 reverses the prior exactly-once Round-A unconditional fan-in to apply effective applicability to activated project criteria while preserving one-execution semantics.

RP-06 failed/cancelled/shed units never persist success checkpoints; transient failures currently become [] and suppress later healthy calls, which is corrected; parity-first current-run failure projection or posture-aware normalization and explicit authored budget enforcement remain as pending maintainer choices.

All behavior changes are explicitly classified as PRESERVE, APPROVED DELTA, or CHOICE PENDING in the decision audit; cross-RP constraints are RP-03 depends on RP-02 and RP-04, RP-04 supplies RP-01/RP-03/RP-05 authority, and RP-06 can migrate through stable runner seam without hard tracker dependency.
